warnings: House title block: '(026) บ้านพู่ระหง' — 'แบบบ้านยิ้มเพื่อประชาชน' series, สำนักการโยธา กรุงเทพมหานคร (same series/program as houses already in the dataset e.g. 024/028 ธรรมรักษา). Small 2-story house, single-span 3x3 column grid (7.80x7.80m main bay), all-steel hip roof (จันทัน C-100x50x20x2.3mm@1.00m, ระแนงสำเร็จรูป@0.32-0.34m, ตะเข้สัน/สัน 2C-150x50x20x3.2mm) over an RC frame.

Dummy row A' (0.50m north of grid A) is required by a real beam endpoint: beams B2 and CB3 on the ground-floor beam plan (S-02/หน้า18) form a small kitchen bump-out that projects north of the main A-B-C bay. Position 0.50m is printed identically on both the structural sheet (S-02) and the architectural ground-floor plan (A-03/หน้า04).

Dummy column 1' (~2.25m east of grid 1) is required by a real beam endpoint: an interior 'B1' beam on both S-02 floor plans (หน้า18) separates the stairwell/duct void from the adjacent room, and does not sit on any main grid line. NO sheet in this house's structural set prints a horizontal dimension for this interior line. Position 2.25m is carried over from the architectural stair detail (A-14/หน้า15, ground-floor stair-expansion plan), which prints '9 ลูกนอนๆ@0.25=2.25ม.' as the stair run starting at grid 1 — the best available evidence, but it is a cross-sheet inference, not a value printed on any structural sheet itself. Recorded with a lowered per-line confidence_score (0.35) and flagged here rather than silently guessing or dropping the beam (per the beam-endpoint rule).

S-02 (หน้า18) prints a second, unrelated horizontal dimension west of grid 1: '0.50' then a separate parallel '1.50' (not additive/chained — confirmed two independent dimension lines by comparing tick-mark pairs). The architectural ground-floor plan (A-03/หน้า04) prints the same '0.50' but its second dimension reads '1.80', not '1.50' — a genuine discrepancy between the structural and architectural sheets for what appears to be the same ซักล้าง (wash area) extension west of grid 1. Neither figure lands on a beam endpoint (the ซักล้าง/ที่จอดรถ appendage west of grid 1 is a slab-on-grade 'GS' area per DETAIL GS on S-04, with only minor B0 tie-beams of unresolved exact position around door openings) so no dummy grid was created for either reading; both numbers are recorded in unassigned_dimensions and this conflict is flagged per the standing precedence rule (never silently pick one) rather than resolved, since the appendage is architectural, not part of the main structural bay.

Roof-frame plan (S-03/หน้า19) prints a full-perimeter 1.30m eave overhang beyond all four sides of the main 7.80x7.80 grid box (จันทัน rafters cantilever past grid 1/3/A/C). No discrete beam mark terminates at the overhang edge (B9/B1 roof-level ties all land on the main grid or on dummy A'); rafters/purlins are spacing-based repeated members with no individual grid_ref, matching the established precedent (house 12/024) of not inventing a dummy grid for a repeating member's reach. Recorded as 4 unassigned_dimensions entries instead.

op04 scope note: z_levels is sparse (only the ±0.00 site datum from the F1/F2 pile sections on S-05/หน้า21) because op04 does not extract elevation/section (side_profile) sheets, which is where this house's full floor-level chain (+0.50 ground floor, +3.70 upper floor per the A-14 stair section) is actually printed. This is a known, deliberate scope limitation, not a missed read — see _scope.json.

Pile length is printed as '0.18x0.18x16.00m.' (SAFE LOAD 15 T./PILE) identically on both the F1 and F2 detail sections (S-05/หน้า21), re-verified at 4x zoom on the digit string. 16.00m is unusually long for a 180x180mm precast pile on a small 2-story house but is legible and consistent across both callouts, so it is transcribed as printed rather than 'corrected' to a more typical 6.00m.

confidence_flags: position not printed on any structural sheet; carried over from architectural stair-run dimension on A-14/หน้า15 — see file warnings

position estimated as the visual B-C midpoint; not printed on any sheet — introduced only because beam CB5 (S-02/หน้า18) T-intersects the interior 1' partition line and, per the beam-endpoint/beam-bears-on-beam split rule, that intersection needs a name. See file warnings on หน้า18_view1_plan_beam_floor1.json
